clue.text: Dora's protégé

parts.note: DORA was the Defence of the ... Act of 1914, so what DORA protects is the kingdom it was passed to defend

explanation.surface: A young person taken under the wing of a woman called Dora.
explanation.walkthrough: Dora looks like a woman's name, but DORA is the wartime British Defence of the Realm Act; the thing it shields is the kingdom itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is the thing a defence act sets out to protect, so it is the act's ward.

clue.text: Respected members of Peru board

indicators.note: the letters are the members of the word, taken apart and rearranged

parts.note: a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Esteemed members of a Peruvian governing board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members of' rearranges PERU into REPU, then TABLE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Of good standing and honourable character.

clue.text: Violin-maker appears soon 'after midnight

parts.note: am stands for ante meridiem, the hours after midnight
soon after midnight is at one o'clock, written AT I with the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A violin-maker shows up in the early hours.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says he appears in the small hours; read as a time, it is a.m. at I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: The Amati family of Cremona were celebrated violin-makers before Stradivari.

clue.text: White slave brings mule formation into force

indicators.note: into puts one piece inside another

parts.note: to make someone do something is to force them

indicators.note: formation means the letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: A slave drives a mule into line by force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation' rearranges MULE into MELU, and 'into' puts that inside MAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mamelukes of Egypt were a caste of soldiers who began as white slaves from the Caucasus.

clue.text: Where the seed might get set on grass?

definitions.text: Where the seed might get set on grass?

parts.words: Where the seed might get set on grass
parts.note: seeds here are ranked tennis players and a set is part of a match, played at the famous grass-court championship in south-west London

explanation.surface: A gardener wondering where to sow seed on a lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Seed and grass suggest gardening; in tennis a seeded player plays sets, and the great grass-court tournament is held in a London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: The All England Club's grass courts host seeded tennis players losing and winning sets each summer.

clue.text: Carry on working for it

definitions.meaning: to conduct or pursue, as in carrying on a war
the pay earned from a job

explanation.surface: Keep going, you are earning it.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to conduct a campaign or war; the other is pay earned by labour.

clue.text: Household tries decapitation of lots of animals

parts.note: menage is a household

indicators.note: decapitation removes the head, so the first letter goes

explanation.surface: A household attempts to behead a great many animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitation' drops T, the head of TRIES, leaving RIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Collections of wild beasts kept for exhibition, a zoo's worth of creatures.

clue.text: Clear view of one member in a hat

indicators.note: in puts the pieces inside the other

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A clear view of a politician wearing a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I and MP inside LID. 'view of' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Transparent and unclouded, like still water.

clue.text: Very severe on Scot, following overdraft

parts.note: an overdrawn account is DR A/C, debit account
taken as written
Ian is a typical Scots name

explanation.surface: A harsh line on a Scotsman with an overdraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' says ON and IAN come after DRAC; DR is debit and AC account.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh, after Draco, the Athenian lawgiver whose penalties were notoriously cruel.

clue.text: Unpleasant erection of an eyesore

indicators.note: in a down clue erecting a word sets it upright, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sty is an ugly, filthy place

explanation.surface: Building an ugly structure is distasteful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erection of' turns AN into NA, before STY.
explanation.definitionFit: Disagreeable or offensive in nature.

clue.text: Bird as paying guest, Martian sort

indicators.note: to sort things is to rearrange them, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: PG is the standard abbreviation for a paying guest, a lodger

explanation.surface: A Martian lodging somewhere as a paying guest, who is some kind of bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' rearranges PG and MARTIAN together into the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a grouse of mountain and Arctic regions that turns white in winter.

clue.text: Intends to support us ?

definitions.meaning: our financial resources, what we live on, as in 'living beyond your'

explanation.surface: Someone who plans to keep us going.
explanation.definitionFit: Intends is a verb sense; the noun sense is income or resources that keep a person going.

clue.text: He leaves the brooks with sounds of bird-song

indicators.note: something that leaves goes away, so these letters are taken out of the phrase that follows

parts.note: rills are small streams, the same as brooks
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man walks away from the streams, hearing birdsong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes HE out of THE RILLS, leaving T plus RILLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds warble in rapid quavering notes, which is what a run of these is.

clue.text: Takes great pains about border plant

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: agony is great pain
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A gardener taking great pains over a plant for the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts AGONY round RIM. 'border' feels like the garden bed, but it gives the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrimony is a yellow-flowered herb of the rose family.

clue.text: Point to American retirement pay hold-up

parts.note: S is south, a point of the compass
a pension is pay in retirement

explanation.surface: A complaint about delays to American retirement payments.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'hold-up' is a delay; as definition it is a stoppage or interruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary stoppage or interruption, as of play or business.

clue.text: Scoundrel's look-out for Drummond's gang

parts.note: in Sapper's novel The Black Gang, Bulldog Drummond leads a vigilante band, so his gang is the Black one
a guard keeps look-out

explanation.surface: A villain posted as sentry for a fictional adventurer's gang.
explanation.walkthrough: Bulldog Drummond is a hero of 1920s British thrillers; his band of vigilantes was the Black Gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A villainous rogue, an old word for a man without honour.

clue.text: Article on the German master race written in Swiss resort

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
der is German for the
MA is a Master of Arts
the TT, Tourist Trophy, is a motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A news article about German racial theory penned in a Swiss resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'written in' join the pieces; the TT is the famous Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: A village and ski resort in the canton of Uri near the Gotthard Pass.

clue.text: Compact city house perhaps

definitions.meaning: a business, a commercial house of the kind found in the City of London

explanation.surface: A small townhouse that is snug.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is solid and unyielding; the other is a company, a trading house in the City.

clue.text: Revolver the main danger in Poe's' tale?

definitions.text: Revolver the main danger in Poe's' tale?

parts.words: Revolver the main danger in Poe's' tale
parts.note: a revolver is something that spins, and the main is the sea; Poe wrote of a descent into a great whirlpool

explanation.surface: A gun being the main threat in an Edgar Allan Poe story.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolver suggests a pistol and main the chief; read them as a spinning thing and the sea, the subject of Poe's A Descent into the Maelström.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent whirlpool at sea, a revolving danger to ships, the subject of a Poe story.

clue.text: Announce the player's demand?

parts.note: a pro is a professional player
a claim is a demand

explanation.surface: Publicising what a sportsman wants.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO is the professional player, and CLAIM his demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare publicly and officially.

clue.text: Their meeting indicates a successful economy

definitions.text: Their meeting indicates a successful economy

parts.words: Their meeting indicates a successful economy
parts.note: the idiom about making both extremes of the budget meet, managing income and spending

explanation.surface: A remark about two people whose meeting shows a thriving economy.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'make ends meet' means to manage on what you have.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of household budgeting is to make these two extremities meet.

clue.text: Look for a soft fruit with the new cane

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Shopping for a soft fruit along with a new walking cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CANE into ANCE, which ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: How something looks, its outward aspect.

clue.text: Replacement of Master Morgan's flasher

indicators.note: replacing the letters puts them in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone replacing a schoolmaster called Morgan, who exposed himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Morgan's 1938 play The Flashing Stream gives the definition; 'Replacement of' rearranges MASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Morgan wrote a play called The Flashing Stream, so the flashing thing in his work is a brook.

clue.text: Singer gives Robin tea in resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, sorting again, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vocalist treats a man called Robin to tea at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in resort' looks like a seaside place but means re-sorted: ROBIN TEA is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A male voice between tenor and bass, or a man who sings in it.

clue.text: Note, on lioness raised in Switzerland

parts.note: B is a musical note

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Elsa is the lioness of Born Free

explanation.surface: A note about a lioness reared in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ELSA into ASLE, after B.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on the Rhine is Basel, a place in the Swiss north.

clue.text: Hood is aboard — looks 'angry

indicators.note: is with aboard says the hood is on the ship, placed within it

parts.note: aboard means on a ship, and SS is the abbreviation for steamship
a cowl is a monk's hood

explanation.surface: Hood is on the ship looking furious, perhaps a naval commander.
explanation.walkthrough: Hood sounds like a naval admiral or warship, but it is a cowl. Being aboard means inside SS, the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Frowns with displeasure; furrowed brows are a sign of anger.

clue.text: The god of poetry, in certain quarters

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: W and N are west and north, two quarters of the compass
an ode is a poem

explanation.surface: Some regard him as the god of poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ODE between W and N. 'of' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief Anglo-Saxon deity, equivalent of Norse Odin, who gave Wednesday its name.

clue.text: Experienced hat-maker ?

definitions.meaning: a matted fabric from which hats are made

explanation.surface: A seasoned milliner.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is sensed or underwent; the other is matted wool cloth for making trilbies.

clue.text: Fish connected with 'the sole?

definitions.meaning: a flat fish of the ray family
a blade or wheels fixed to the sole of a boot for gliding on ice or rinks

explanation.surface: A fish linked to another flatfish, the sole.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray is a sea creature of that name; the other sense is a boot with a blade attached under the foot.

clue.text: Native put dash of French in poor cider.

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
poor signals the letters are badly made, so they are reworked

parts.note: elan is a French word for dash or verve

explanation.surface: A local adds a French flourish to some poor cider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges CIDER into ICDER, and 'in' puts ELAN between IC and DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born on the North Atlantic island nation, one of its natives.

clue.text: Meets anti-reformer in café

indicators.note: a reformer changes things, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An opponent of reform has a meeting in a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anti-reformer' reads as a political conservative, but ANTI is fodder and 'reformer' rearranges MEETS ANTI.
explanation.definitionFit: A small French bar or bistro serving drinks.

clue.text: A drop in the bar ?

definitions.meaning: the smallest unit of liquid measure, about one drop
a musical note, a half note, found in a bar of music

explanation.surface: Someone having a drink at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an apothecaries' fluid measure of one drop; the other a half-note in music.
